interest: This document provides valuable administrative and historical insight into how the United States monitored intra-imperial labor migration within the Japanese Empire during the 1930s. Although only the docket sheet ('List of Papers') is preserved here, it details four reports tracking the flow of Korean laborers to Japan, Japanese regulatory restrictions, and local press discourse in both Chosen and Tokyo. Furthermore, the file records early diplomatic reporting by prominent Foreign Service figures, notably future ambassador John M. Allison and Consul William R. Langdon, illustrating how American observers drew comparisons between East Asian migration dynamics and immigration policies in the United States and Canada.
overview: This file consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet for U.S. State Department decimal file 894.5595, documenting American diplomatic monitoring of Korean immigration into Japan in 1934. The sheet catalogues four communications originating from or handled by the American Consulate General in Seoul, the Embassy in Tokyo, and the State Department's Visa Division. These documents address the social and economic drivers of Korean labor migration to the Japanese mainland, statistical records and local demand for Korean labor, measures and regulations enacted to restrict this migration, and contemporary coverage in the Korean and Japanese press.

subfiles.about: A State Department docket sheet listing four despatches and reports from 1934 concerning Korean immigration and labor movements into Japan.
subfiles.summary: This sub-file serves as the State Department index and docket sheet for decimal file 894.5595 ('Immigration To Japan From Chosen'). It summarizes four separate items from 1934: Despatch No. 22 from Consul William R. Langdon in Seoul regarding Korean emigration and related social/economic factors; a Visa Division memorandum by John Farr Simmons enclosing Korean press translations and labor statistics; Report No. 143 from John M. Allison in Tokyo examining restrictions on Korean migration; and Allison's Report No. 148 detailing migratory trends in response to a departmental circular. Together, these entries outline the scope of American reporting on Korean labor migration to Japan and official Japanese efforts to control it.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Immigration to Japan from Chosen
